title: Example plugin settings
description: Ship one of these and the admin UI renders a real form for your settings instead of a raw text editor. Without it an operator edits your config.toml by hand. Every property here matches a key in config.toml; delete the ones you do not need.

greeting.title: Greeting
greeting.description: What the hello tool says. This description is the help text an operator reads, so write it for them rather than for yourself.
greeting.default: Hello from the PersonaCore plugin template.

excitement.title: Exclamation marks
excitement.description: How many to add. The bounds are enforced by the form, so an operator cannot save a value your code would reject.

shout.title: Shout it
shout.description: A boolean becomes a toggle. This one is here to show the control; delete it with the rest.

tone.title: Tone
tone.description: A string with enum becomes a dropdown.

x-personacore-notes: KEYS ARE FLAT. The form renders top-level properties and repeating groups.
It does NOT render a plain nested object as a sub-section, so a config.toml
with [some.section] headings gets the raw editor instead of a form. Keep your
settings flat and obviously named unless you specifically want a repeating
group.
THE CORE RENDERS A BOUNDED VOCABULARY AND NEVER EXECUTES ANYTHING FROM A
SCHEMA. That is a security boundary, not a limitation: your schema is data
supplied by a third party, so it is read and never run. Keywords outside the
set below are ignored rather than obeyed.
The controls, and what produces each:
toggle           type: boolean
dropdown         type: string with enum
number           type: integer or number, with minimum / maximum
text             type: string, with minLength / maxLength
long text        type: string with x-personacore-multiline: true
list of strings  type: array of strings
secret picker    type: string with x-personacore-secret: true
-- offers the NAMES of stored secrets, never a value.
Declare the name in manifest.toml permissions.secrets.
repeating group  type: object with additionalProperties describing one entry
-- several fields per entry, each named by the operator.
SEARCH-AND-FILL. Any field can be filled by searching rather than typing. Add
x-personacore-lookup naming one of your own tools; the operator types a query,
picks a result, and one or more fields fill in. It is a general mechanism
available to any plugin -- weather is simply the first to use it.
For repeating groups and search-and-fill together, read
plugins/weather/config.schema.json. It is the worked example for both.
A field with a default shows it marked AS a default, so an operator can tell
'the plugin is using this' from 'the plugin would use this if you saved'.
You still validate your settings when you load them. The form stops the
obviously wrong ones; it does not know what your settings MEAN.
